content: This document provides detailed information about the medication ganciclovir, which is used to treat herpes infections of the eye. While ganciclovir effectively inhibits the growth of the herpes virus, it does not cure the infection, as the virus remains dormant in the body between outbreaks. This medication is classified as an antiviral drug and is specifically designed to treat herpes eye infections. It is not effective against other types of eye infections, such as those caused by bacteria. Instructions for Use: Before applying the medication, wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while you have an eye infection or are using this medication. To apply the eye drops, tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. This helps prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes after application. Do not rinse the dropper. If you are using other eye medications, wait at least 5 minutes between applications. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. To help you remember, apply it at the same times each day. Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Temporary blurred vision and mild eye irritation or redness may occur after applying the medication. These effects are usually not serious. However, remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Precautions: Before using ganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to valganciclovir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred, so avoid driving or operating machinery until your vision clears. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as its effects on an unborn child are not fully known. It is also unclear whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions, so consult your healthcare provider for more information. Overdose: If someone swallows this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature and protect it from freezing. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. Important Notes: This document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments, as tests such as eye exams may be conducted while you are using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and ask for clarification if needed.
